events.title: The election of Pope St. Hilarius
events.shortBlurb: Leo the Great's archdeacon, who had barely escaped the Robber Council of Ephesus, was raised nine days after his master's death to the chair of Peter…
body: Hilarius, a native of Sardinia, had served as archdeacon of the Roman Church and as a legate of Pope Leo I. At the tumultuous Second Council of Ephesus in 449 — the "Robber Synod" that upheld the heresiarch Eutyches — he protested against its violence and fled for his life, afterward standing among the defenders of the Council of Chalcedon.

Nine days after the death of Leo the Great, on 19 November 461, Hilarius was consecrated bishop of Rome. He carried forward his master's policies with vigor, held Roman synods in 462 and 465, and labored to set the churches of Gaul and Spain in order, settling disputes over jurisdiction among their bishops and upholding the discipline of the metropolitans.
In Rome he adorned the churches, and is remembered especially for the oratories he added to the Lateran baptistery. He died on 29 February 468 and is venerated as a saint of the Church.
